title: GM EV: Precharge Time Too Long, check the 12 V battery first

applies_to.scope_note: First described for the Chevrolet Bolt EV 2018. The expert then extended it to all GM electric vehicles of 2018-2025. Only the Bolt EV is named from direct experience; the wider scope is his generalisation and is not verified per model.

symptoms: May appear after a collision, or with no collision

claims.text: A weak or discharged 12 V battery can cause 'Precharge time too long' and stop the vehicle entering READY, with or without a collision.
After a collision the 12 V battery is usually discharged, so the fault can remain even after the collision repair.
Jump-starting (booster cables) did not solve it in the cases he met. A healthy, charged 12 V battery must be fitted and connected correctly.
The point is a healthy, charged, correctly installed battery, not a battery stronger than the factory specification.
claims.note: The expert corrected the assistant on this.

claims.text: After collision repair, an Impact Reset is done through inverter number 2 with a scan tool that supports the function.
claims.note: The part of the conversation where he described this is not in the file. The exact function name is not confirmed.

claims.text: Measure the 12 V battery voltage during the start attempt before suspecting the inverter or the high-voltage contactors.

warnings: After a collision, confirm the high-voltage system is intact before any reset or start attempt.
